key_insight: Pressure tunes ferroelectric LaMoN3 from a 2.17 eV to 1.45 eV indirect gap and creates an optimal mid-pressure window for improved photovoltaic and nonlinear optical response.
engineering_relevance: This suggests pressure-engineered nitride perovskites could be designed as absorber layers in multi-junction solar devices to combine stronger linear absorption with enhanced shift-current-based efficiency.
method: First-principles DFT and DFPT to assess structural and dynamical stability up to 40 GPa
Many-body perturbation theory (G0W0 and BSE) to compute bandgap, excitons, and optical response
Tight-binding analysis to interpret pressure-driven electronic structure trends
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that LaMoN3 remains dynamically stable to 40 GPa, while the G0W0@PBE bandgap narrows and BSE shows pressure increases SLME and lowers exciton binding energy, with bulk photovoltaic efficiency peaking near 15 GPa.
watch_item: The main implementation challenge is that the strongest performance gains are pressure-dependent, so translating the results into practical devices will require a feasible way to stabilize or emulate the optimal phase conditions.
paper_title: Harnessing Linear and Nonlinear Optical Responses in Ferroelectric LaMoN$_3$ for Enhanced Photovoltaic Efficiency
